_comment: CORRECTIONS to expected routes that a question set defines wrongly or incompletely.
This is the second of two route overlays, and the two have opposite jobs:
expected-routes-g-i.json         FILLS a route in where the set defines none. Never overrides.
expected-routes-corrections.json (this file) OVERRIDES a route the set does define, where that
route is wrong, or names only some of the legitimate ways to
reach the answer.
WHY AN OVERLAY AND NOT AN EDIT. A runset is the file a recorded run was measured with, and editing
it makes the recorded figures unreproducible from the thing that produced them. So runsets stay
byte-identical and corrections are applied at scoring time: a rescore with this file present
reports what the run SHOULD have scored, while the result document keeps saying what it DID score.
Anyone comparing the two needs to know which is which - so a correction that changes a published
number must be called out wherever that number is published.
WHEN A CORRECTION IS WARRANTED. Only when the route is wrong about the codebase. 'The model
reached the answer another way' is a finding about the model; 'the route we wrote down was not the
only correct one' is a defect in the set. State which, and what you checked, in the entry.
KEYED BY QUESTION ID, SO IT ONLY MEANS ANYTHING AGAINST THE SET THOSE IDS CAME FROM. Ids are reused
across sets - Q008 in this repository's seed set is a different question from Q008 in the set that
produced the published figures - so an entry carried from one set to another silently overrides an
unrelated question with a route naming classes its project does not contain. That is a wrong answer
key, which is the failure this harness has published and corrected twice. Write entries against the
set you are measuring, and do not copy them between sets.
THIS FILE SHIPS EMPTY on purpose. Entries belong to a tree and its question set, not to the tool.
Record every entry in QUESTION-DEFECTS.md as well, which is the human-readable changelist, and keep
the two in step.
SHAPE. One key per question id, whose value is the corrected route string. Keys beginning with an
underscore are ignored, so a per-entry rationale lives beside its entry as "_Q008": [ ... ].
